title: ALL CAPS: THE HISTORY OF THE AMERICAN BASEBALL HAT
chaptersLine: Forty-plus chapters drafted, plus an introduction and a closing coda.
spanLine: From before the Civil War to the drops of 2026.
thisWeek: The voice pass kept moving this week, with the master manuscript touched again on Friday.
A long-flagged language question got run down and cleared, the kind of small true thing this book likes to chase.
The weekly research scan pulled in two fresh, chapter-keyed notes, both quietly folded into the pile.
chapterHighlights: The house band nobody expects: a two-man crew that scored an entire imaginary baseball league for one hat shop.
The grail caps you cannot buy, hand-numbered and built from a fabric that no longer exists.
Why the most famous cap company on earth is not the biggest, and what that gap is really about.
The one season a legendary blue franchise went green for luck, and the cap that proves it happened.
